ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, including amendments introduced by Law No. 154 of 2022; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 951 of 2003, as amended; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, and its Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended; Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; applicable Financial Regulatory Authority and Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit rules; GAFI and Commercial Registry beneficial-owner and shareholder-identification requirements. Egypt does not operate a universally public, fully searchable UBO register equivalent to a public corporate ownership database.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder or individual investor, authenticated by a competent notary or Egyptian consular authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and throughout the relationship, identify and screen all direct and indirect shareholders, UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, agents, and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, United States OFAC lists, applicable European Union and United Kingdom sanctions where relevant, Egyptian domestic sanctions and terrorism lists, and reputable PEP, relatives-and-close-associates databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, state-owned entities, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque trusts, nominee arrangements, cash-intensive businesses, adverse media, unexplained wealth, and complex ownership chains. Obtain documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, establish approval and escalation controls, retain records for the statutory period, and file suspicious-transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit where legally required. Stripe and PayPal onboarding may impose additional global sanctions, KYC, beneficial-owner, chargeback, consumer-protection, and prohibited-business controls.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic incorporation and services portal, accessed through the official GAFI website at https://www.gafi.gov.eg; final registration and name verification are coordinated with the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must comply with Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and GAFI naming rules, be distinguishable from existing registered names, and not mislead the public regarding activity, ownership, governmental affiliation, nationality, or legal form. Arabic is required for official Egyptian filings; a foreign-language or transliterated version may be used only if accepted by GAFI and the Commercial Registry. The name should include or clearly indicate the legal form, such as Limited Liability Company or its accepted Arabic equivalent. Arabic translations and certified translations are required for foreign-language supporting documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Egyptian governmental, ministerial, military, judicial, diplomatic, or public-authority designations without approval
Words implying sovereign, governmental, royal, military, banking, insurance, financing, securities, investment-fund, or regulated financial status without the required license or approval
Religious or politically sensitive terms that could create public-order or misleading-association concerns
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, trademark, trade name, or protected institutional name
Geographical or international organization names implying official affiliation without approval
Terms suggesting a licensed profession, university, hospital, pharmaceutical, telecommunications, customs, shipping, or other regulated activity without sector approval
Offensive, deceptive, public-order-sensitive, or contrary-to-law expressions
The words 'bank', 'insurance', 'exchange', 'finance', 'securities', 'investment', and equivalent Arabic expressions unless the competent regulator has granted the required approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain written or electronic rejection reasons from GAFI or the Commercial Registry; preserve the application reference, rejected name, proposed activity, and supporting evidence; submit a corrected name or formal reconsideration request through the same GAFI service channel within the applicable administrative period; attach evidence of distinctiveness, trademark ownership, investor authorization, and any sector approval; escalate unresolved objections to the competent GAFI grievance or review committee and, where appropriate, pursue an administrative appeal before the competent Egyptian administrative court under the State Council Law. A rejected name should not be used in contracts, invoices, payment accounts, advertising, or tax registrations. Legal review is required before judicial escalation because appeal deadlines and the competent forum depend on the form of the challenged administrative act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office and valid Egyptian address are required. A serviced or virtual office may be accepted for a low-risk e-commerce company if the provider permits official registration, maintains lease or occupancy evidence, receives governmental correspondence, and satisfies GAFI, Commercial Registry, Tax Authority, bank, payment processor, and AML verification requirements. A virtual office is not sufficient where the business stores inventory, imports goods, employs personnel, conducts regulated activities, or requires operational premises. For pet-supplies e-commerce, the company must accurately disclose the absence or presence of warehouse, fulfillment, import, veterinary, product-safety, and animal-health activities. Importing veterinary medicines, animal feed, live animals, or regulated devices may trigger additional licenses despite ordinary retail e-commerce not generally requiring a sector license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official Egyptian statistical probability of unannounced inspection is published. Internal risk assessment: approximately 10% to 20% annual likelihood for a newly incorporated, low-risk, non-regulated e-commerce entity with complete tax, lease, AML, and corporate records; materially higher if the registered address is a nominal mailbox, tax filings are inconsistent, payment activity is unusual, inventory is held at an undisclosed location, or the business imports regulated pet products. The estimate is not a statutory probability and must not be represented as an official government metric.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 194 of 2020 promulgating the Egyptian Companies Law (successor to Law 159/1981) and its Executive Regulations under Decree No. 55 of 2022, LLC incorporation, capital, manager, Commercial Registry, and registration chapters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Investor Services Center / One-Stop Shop (OSS); Commercial Registry directorate of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: GAFI electronic Declaration of Establishment together with the Model Articles of Association; the statutory proof is the Certificate of Incorporation (Sijil Qayd al-Sharika) issued through the GAFI OSS, with the Commercial Registry extract as an integral annex.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an LLC under Companies Law 194/2020 and Executive Regulations 55/2022; the Articles freely fix the subscribed capital (commonly EGP 50,000). The capital must be deposited in an Egyptian bank account 'under formation' and a bank certificate evidencing the deposit is filed with GAFI; the account is released to the Company upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and no escrow account is maintained beyond registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation documents and the Articles of Association of the Company, as filed with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, are approved and ratified. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the share capital stated in the Articles is subscribed, and the founders' subscription declarations are accepted. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office address in the Articles is adopted, the head-office lease is ratified, and the Manager is authorized to amend registry entries accordingly. RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the Manager and authorized signatories are appointed with full power to complete incorporation, to operate bank accounts, and to act in the statutory registration of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and permissible-activity confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (NAFEZA) e-portal - company name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name in Arabic and Latin scripts and verify that ISIC 4791 (electronic retail of pet supplies) is an accepted commercial activity code. The request is decided within 3 business days; the approved name is reserved for the statutory period and will appear in the Articles and all later filings.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation request with three alternative names
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On conflict with a registered name or mark, the request is refused with reasons; submit a new name or file an appeal with the GAFI investor complaints/ombudsman unit within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authentication of the Articles of Association and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice commercial notary; Central Bank of Egypt-licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders or their attorneys appear before the commercial notary for authentication of the signed Arabic Articles and ensure fiscal stamps are affixed. The stated share capital is deposited into a bank account 'under formation', and the bank issues the capital certificate that will be uploaded to GAFI. No blocked/escrow account is required once incorporation is completed.
required_dossiers: Authenticated Articles of Association (Arabic) in the number of copies required by the notary
Notarized powers of attorney for absent founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the file for a clause correction, amend the clause electronically and re-schedule attestation; if the bank cannot issue the certificate on the same day, request a temporary letter and replace it before the GAFI submission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - unified national tax administration operating via the ETA digital portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg and the E-Invoice/E-Receipt platforms at https://einvoices.eta.gov.eg; customs export verification coordinated with the Egyptian Customs Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident owned Egyptian LLC: (1) incorporate the LLC and obtain the Commercial Registry extract and Arabic legalized Articles of Association; (2) appoint a resident legal representative and execute a notarized power of attorney; (3) file the Unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) application with the competent ETA office or through the ETA online portal, submitting the incorporation documents, lease or deed of the commercial premises, passports of directors/shareholders, and an estimate of annual turnover; (4) the ETA issues one unified TIN covering corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding, and stamp tax obligations. No minimum capital requirement applies for LLC formation; apostilled foreign documents are accepted following Egypt's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists. Available statutory elections: (1) fiscal unity (group consolidation) with ETA approval, requiring at least 85% direct or indirect ownership; (2) foreign tax credit election computed on a per-country/overall basis; (3) optional cash-basis/simplified accounting for small taxpayers under the CIT threshold; (4) exporters may elect monthly refund of input VAT on zero-rated exports, subject to ETA financial standards.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations; supplementary selective consumption tax not applicable to pet products.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration; e-commerce activities are in scope once an Egyptian fixed establishment exists, irrespective of the foreign merchant's home country threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing under ETA Decision No. 251 of 2020 (and subsequent roadmap): VAT-registered taxpayers must generate invoices in XML/JSON, submit them to the ETA clearance server via API, FTP, or the ETA portal, and print or transmit a cryptographic QR code validated by the ETA. The e-receipt system applies to B2C transactions. Non-compliant invoices are rejected before issuance; penalties may reach EGP 50,000 per invoice, with suspension of the taxpayer's VAT certificate for chronic violations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of physical pet supplies qualifies for the 0% VAT rate if: (a) the exporter is VAT-registered in Egypt; (b) the goods are transported out of Egyptian customs territory; (c) the buyer is a non-resident; (d) the export declaration is released by Egyptian Customs; and (e) the sale is documented by the export invoice, transport document, and foreign currency remittance. Offshore services to foreign principals may qualify if the economic benefit is realized outside Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form C91 outbound release)
Commercial Invoice matching customs value and description
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure from Egyptian customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from the Egyptian banking system confirming receipt of foreign currency
ETA export transaction ledger or zero-rating substantiation worksheet
Valid Egyptian unified TIN certificate of the exporting LLC
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA cross-matches e-invoice zero-rated sales against Egyptian Customs outbound declarations and the banking FX remittance database. On fraudulent or unrepatriated export claims, the ETA retrospectively claws back VAT at 14% on the unduly zero-rated supply, adds late payment interest of 2% per month on arrears, imposes an evasion penalty between EGP 5,000 and EGP 50,000 per invoice (or up to 3x the tax evaded), suspends the exporter's VAT registration, commences criminal prosecution carrying imprisonment of no less than 3 years, holds the legal representative personally liable, and may publish the offender's name under tax evasion Law No. 53 of 2014; the Customs Authority may also seize the goods or impose customs fines in case of false export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Foreign Exchange Administration and Banking Supervision; the CBE is the sole monetary and FX regulator, with investment registration coordination executed through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) under the Ministry of Investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined flexible exchange-rate regime for the Egyptian Pound (EGP), formally anchored since March 2024 under the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account transactions are fully convertible: trade settlements, service payments, royalties, and profit/dividend remittances do not require prior CBE approval, provided the transaction is executed through a CBE-licensed authorized dealer bank with standard underlying documentation (contracts, invoices, audited financial statements, and tax-clearance certificates) and is coded under the CBE's Economic Purpose Code (EPC) framework. Capital-account inflows are substantially liberalized: foreign direct investment equity injections, shareholder loans, and investment loans may be routed through authorized banks and benefit from Egypt's inward-remittance registration regime, which formally evidences legal repatriation rights. Residual practical hurdles include FX liquidity management: during tight-liquidity windows, banks may queue outbound remittance requests; however, no de jure convertibility restriction or repatriation tax levy applies. Profit remittance requires the prior year's audited balance sheet, proof of tax registration and corporate income-tax compliance, and the historical inward-remittance registration certificate; dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders applies at 10% domestically (5% for qualifying treaty residents) and must be deducted and declared. Overall rating: full convertibility for e-commerce operating flows, with strict documentary discipline and bank-level liquidity rationing as the only operational constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE's export-proceeds directive, as amended through 2022 and maintained unchanged after the March 2024 flexible-exchange reform, Egyptian exporters — including e-commerce merchants selling pet products cross-border — must: (1) receive all export receipts through a licensed Egyptian bank; (2) repatriate the full invoice value through the banking system within 180 days from the date of issuance of the bill of lading or airway bill; and (3) deliver to the bank a customs export declaration, a validated Export Confirmation (Form No. 2), a commercial invoice, and shipping documents for each consignment. There is NO mandatory conversion ratio: a 0% statutory surrender requirement applies, meaning exporters may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in a corporate FX account, convert to EGP at the freely floating market rate, or apply the proceeds to lawful import payments and trade obligations, subject to the bank's foreign-currency budget and internal trade-finance underwriting. Export proceeds may not be assigned to offshore accounts or left indefinitely outside Egypt. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline exposes the exporter to penalties under Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, customs-law import-compensation measures, and tax-audit adjustments under the Income Tax Law, in addition to potential AML scrutiny for unexplained offshore balances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (temporary blocked incorporation/capital-deposit account, converted post-registration) / Operational Multi-Currency Account (EGP, USD, EUR)
Capital Deposit Account for LLC formation / Operational EGP and Foreign-Currency Current Accounts with trade-finance limits
Capital Blocked Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account with dedicated FX sub-ledger and e-commerce acquirer integration
Capital Deposit Account / Multi-Currency Corporate Account with HSBCnet digital treasury module
EGP Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Account for trade settlements and cross-border e-commerce receipts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW as a principal banking or settlement rail; MEDIUM only as an ancillary inbound collection aggregator. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex and similar) are not licensed by the CBE and may not hold Egyptian-resident corporate funds, maintain local IBANs, or act as the settlement account for the LLC's export collections, as such activity would breach the CBE licensing perimeter under Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 and the Fintech Law No. 5 of 2022. The permissible boundary is narrow: an offshore EMI may receive card-network payouts from PayPal/Stripe or marketplace channels and consolidate them, then transmit the funds to the LLC's Egyptian bank account via SWIFT MT103 with an accurate purpose code. However, this 'chain-broken' model creates bank-side KYC friction, delayed crediting, and AML reverse-verification risk. For the target payment rails (Stripe and PayPal), the fully compliant structure is: Stripe/PayPal collect customer card payments, where available through a licensed Egyptian acquiring or payment-facilitator arrangement, and settle through a CBE-licensed electronic-payment provider (e.g., PayMob, Telr, or e-finance/Fawry for domestic-credential flows) directly into the LLC's onshore account with a clear e-commerce settlement reason. Standalone offshore digital-banking reliance is not acceptable for statutory accounting, CBE inward-investment registration, or tax documentation purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence. For an Egyptian LLC at any Tier-1 commercial bank, the statutory manager (or, if the memorandum of association appoints multiple joint managers, at least one of them) must appear in person at the designated bank branch where the capital and operational accounts are opened, carrying the original national ID or valid passport. The bank's AML compliance officer will conduct a non-delegable in-person KYC interview covering the UBO structure, commercial model (electronic retailing of pet supplies), expected transaction volumes and jurisdictions, source of funds, and the full beneficiary profile. In practice, banks require the principal manager to attend an initial onboarding interview and a subsequent 'transaction profile' interview before activating high-volume cross-border payment channels. Remote or video-based KYC is not available for LLC corporate accounts at CBE-licensed banks as of the current regulatory position. A representative holding a notarized, translated (if executed abroad) and duly certified power of attorney may perform administrative filings and document delivery, but the first KYC interview and final risk acceptance are conducted with the natural-person manager personally. Foreign non-resident managers must appear with a valid entry visa or business residency, original passport, address verification, and, where requested, a police clearance certificate or source-of-funds affidavit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity fragmented cross-border e-commerce payouts: PayPal/Stripe micro-transactions arriving without a single convertible trade invoice, creating a 'shadow trade flow' red flag at the receiving bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated marketplace settlement reports for the preceding 12 months; PayPal/Stripe merchant service agreements; per-transaction order-ID log linked to customer identity, product type, and delivery address; courier airway bills and shipment manifests (DHL, FedEx, Aramex) with tracking numbers; batch-level customs export declarations (Form No. 2) and commercial invoices; an internal sales ledger showing buyer particulars, product description (pet supplies and pet-care devices), unit pricing, and applicable VAT treatment; and a written narrative mapping the full payment flow from card acquirer to PSP to bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder or UBO opacity and third-country intermediary injection: equity capital arriving through an offshore trust, holding company, or multi-hop correspondent channel, triggering beneficial-ownership verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized, apostilled, and where necessary consular-legalized constitutional documents (Memorandum of Association and Articles); a complete capitalization table tracing to ultimate natural persons; GAFI investment file number and Certificate of Incorporation; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth packages for every subscribing shareholder, including bank statements, tax clearance, and sale/purchase documentation; an Egyptian legal-advocacy AML/KYC opinion confirming the LLC's foreign-direct-investment registration; and a formal UBO declaration signed under Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE AML regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-mirror desynchronization: under-invoicing or over-invoicing red flags detected when invoice values diverge from actual settlement amounts or customs declarations, common in lightly documented e-commerce export models.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export contracts with explicit price lists and Incoterms; insurance certificates and packing lists; bank-offset evidence showing payment-to-invoice matching; customs declarations with harmonized-system commodity codes for pet supplies and pet-care devices; logistics tracking evidence proving physical shipment; and a quarterly reconciliation workbook detailing invoice value, goods value, FX conversion, PSP fees, and final credited amount for every transaction batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hits on buyer names, high-risk country settlement, or name-matching false positives from the target payment rails, causing repeated compliance holds and review referrals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete screening clearance logs generated at onboarding and refreshed at least every 48 hours; registered corporate or individual extracts for recurring high-frequency buyers; negative-media search results and commentary; a self-assessed Customer Risk Rating memo classifying the ebusiness as Low-Risk-Standard under the CBE risk-tiering framework; and a documented AML-CTF response protocol with draft answers to bank queries, supported by the merchant's platform agreements proving the underlying transactions are bona fide consumer pet-products purchases.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for the second leg) from the shareholder's offshore bank to the LLC's inward-equity capital sub-account at the chosen Tier-1 Egyptian bank, with Field 70 Capture containing the reference: '/INST/ EQUITY CAPITAL INJECTION FOR EG LLC, MOA DATED [DATE]' and the CBE External Transaction Nature Code for direct investment equity capital, which the CBE banking guidelines classify under inward direct investment equity participation. The receiving bank requires the following verification pack prior to final credit: Commercial Registry extract showing the LLC and its ISIC 4791 electronic-retailing activity classification; electronic tax registration card; GAFI certificate of incorporation; a board/shareholder resolution (Arabic original or certified translation) authorizing the capital injection and designating the receiving account; passport copies and UBO declarations for each subscriber; and the Foreign Investment Capital Declaration (Form No. 6) through which the CBE records the inward remittance. After verification, the bank issues an Inward Remittance Notice / Certificate of Investment Registration, which constitutes legal evidence of the inward FDI flow and becomes the foundational document supporting future dividend repatriation, capital reduction remittances, and sale-procedure transfer rights. Routing discipline: funds must arrive in a single currency and an amount exactly matching the declared contractual share capital; intermingling with operating revenue is prohibited; the transfer charge allocation must specify 'OUR' to guarantee full value crediting; and any transaction above the bank's high-value threshold (typically USD 1 million or EGP equivalent) triggers immediate EBU/AML referral requiring an accelerated evidence submission. For the e-commerce operating phase, inbound PayPal/Stripe settlements are not treated as capital and must be coded separately as e-commerce goods-export proceeds to preserve clean tax and FX records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are differentiated by value and relationship maturity. Day-to-day supplier settlements for pet-product inventory, packaging, and fulfilment-center fees use SWIFT MT103, with the beneficiary supplier's bank details, a CBE import purpose code (e.g., advanced payment for imports of goods with the relevant HS classification), an invoice/purchase-order reference, and an expected shipment date; standard practice for amounts up to USD 500,000 equivalent favors MT103 for speed and cost. For large-value or first-time counterparties, the rails shift to commercial documentary letters of credit — typically sight L/C or 90-day usance with discounting permission — opened by the LLC's bank at the beneficiary's upstream bank (e.g., HSBC Shanghai for Asian sourcing); Egyptian customs clearing then requires Form No. 4 Customs Declaration through the ECMS system, Certificate of Origin, Commercial Invoice, Bill of Lading, and a certificate of conformity against Egyptian standard requirements. For domestic EGP obligations (VAT payments, payroll, supplier invoices in EGP), the LLC uses the CBE's interbank RTGS and the state e-payment infrastructure (e-taxation and e-payment portals). Outbound Shopify/Amazon marketplace costs paid through Stripe/PayPal are categorized as marketing and payment-processing expenses with supporting platform invoices. All outbound disbursements must be physically matched to a purchase order or contract before execution; any FX conversion to EGP for salary/fixed-cost coverage must be executed on the spot market at the licensed bank's posted rate. Strict prohibitions apply: no cash-based cross-border settlement, no use of unlicensed remittance houses, and no disbursement to third-country shell companies without full commercial and KYC justification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Deliverable FX Forwards — permissible under CBE regulations for trade-backed exposure only (import and export contracts), with tenors from 7 to 360 days, executed at all Tier-1 authorized dealer banks (NBE, Banque Misr, CIB, HSBC Egypt) and supported by underlying shipment or purchase-order documentation.

FX Swaps (value-date and cross-currency) — permissible with CBE-licensed banks for commercial cash-flow liquidity management, used to bridge EGP/FX mismatches between the LLC's import payables and export-receipt timing, with full end-use and beneficiary documentation.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) — permissible where the LLC holds a real financing or long-term asset commitment (e.g., a foreign-shareholder loan or bank term facility), arranged through a CBE-approved swap desk with documented hedge rationale.

European-style FX Options — permissible on a bespoke basis from international desks at HSBC Egypt, CIB, and QNB with CBE derivative-licensing approval; considered advanced and not typically recommended for an SME e-commerce treasury without designated risk-management capacity.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing EGP — NOT permissible for onshore Egyptian resident corporates; participation by the LLC in the offshore EGP NDF market would violate CBE Foreign-Exchange Monopoly rules and Law No. 194/2020, and is therefore excluded from the compliant treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year-end (April 30 for December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EGP 5,000–20,000 and interest on unpaid tax at CBE lending rate plus 2%; enforced collection against company assets; prolonged non-compliance may trigger commercial registry strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end (June 30 for December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EGP 20,000–100,000; after 60-day formal default notice, GAFI may suspend the company's legal status and commence judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the Commercial Registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to EGP 30,000, limitation of legal transactions, and cancellation of commercial registration with potential insolvency proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 100,000–500,000 or imprisonment not exceeding one year for wilful non-disclosure; repeated failure may trigger administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly Minutes and Resolutions Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end and within 30 days after assembly approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors jointly liable for losses caused by delay; court-ordered extraordinary assembly if shareholders so petition; persistent default supports administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for all LLCs under Companies Law No. 194/2020 when paid-in share capital exceeds EGP 250,000 or annual turnover exceeds EGP 1,000,000; foreign-invested LLCs registered under Investment Law No. 72/2017 are required to file audited financial statements with GAFI regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), as issued by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors and largely converging with IFRS; IFRS permitted for an LLC when required by a foreign parent group or upon ETA approval

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must file an annual UBO confirmation with GAFI by March 31 following the reporting fiscal year. Any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, including an aggregate transfer or acquisition exceeding 1% of voting rights, must be updated in the company's UBO register within 30 days. The UBO register must be maintained at the registered office and be available for inspection by GAFI, the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Unit, and judicial authorities upon demand.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 incentives: 50% corporate tax reduction for five years for qualifying projects in underserviced (Zone B/C) governorates; free-zone and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) entities may obtain exemption from income tax on profits from substantive on-site activities in exchange for an annual fee; Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Law No. 152 of 2020 permits an elective presumptive tax regime at a reduced turnover-based rate range (approximately 0.5%-5%) for qualifying small traders; no general offshore e-commerce tax holiday applies.
